algorithm: Raft election compares last term then log length. Followers accept AppendEntries only after a matching prefix. Leaders advance commit for entries in their current term with a majority. Reference: https://raft.github.io/raft.pdf .
architecture: Cluster simulator → typed method RPCs → persistent Node state → committed KV application. Blocked links represent partitions. RPC protocol schema is included for a future transport.
data_model: Node = term, voted_for, log, commit, applied, role, KV. Log entry = term and optional put command. Index zero is a sentinel.
description: A deterministic single-host Raft reference that makes election, replication and partition safety directly inspectable.
design: Never acknowledge an entry before majority commit. Do not truncate committed prefixes. Keep volatile commit state separate from persistent term, vote and log; a restarted follower learns commit from its leader.
family_notes: Commit writes with all three voters available.
Continue with a majority while one follower is down.
Elect a surviving leader after a committed prefix.
Keep a two-node majority while one node is partitioned.
Reject acknowledgments when the leader cannot reach a majority.
Check both old and new majorities for a joint configuration.
limitations: The transport is in-process and deterministic, not a high-concurrency Go/C++ service. There are no real election timers, gRPC server, snapshots, linearizable reads or complete membership-change protocol. The membership workload checks the joint quorum rule only; configuration entries and transition finalization are not implemented. Crash simulation toggles availability, while persistent node restart is checked separately.
operations: Run deterministic failures and inspect each node. Adding network concurrency requires serialized state transitions, deadlines, randomized election timers and a documented read protocol.
scope: Vote freshness, persistent term/vote/log state, matching-prefix append RPCs, conflict truncation, current-term majority commits, committed state-machine application, crash/partition simulation and a joint-quorum predicate.
security: Treat this as educational code; review it before handling trusted data.
title: Key-Value Store with Raft Consensus
